the tile quantum is m*4 = 64; 15 of every 64 pixel-rows are zeros
one core, L1-resident, row-major: 5176 cyc/step vs 4096 ideal

cycles the core spends around the matmuls rather than in them: an operand lock pair every k-step, plus clearing the f32 accumulator and converting it out once per output tile. Running the real 3-tiles x 12-steps nest gives 6271 cyc/step against 6111. zero_vectorized and convert_copy carry their own event markers, so the trace prices them directly: [390, 1292, 1293] cycles once per tile

the gap between one core running the real loop and the 32-core array's steady state. Candidates are inter-core contention for L2/DRAM and the shim-DMA programming the probe does not reproduce, but this experiment does not separate them: it is a residual, not an attribution

a = 85 us, the work-independent intercept of latency = a + b*W over a C_out sweep (R2 = 0.9998); launch_floor.py reproduces it at 85 us on an independent sweep. Note the model only holds for THIS configuration: on the plain mapping the same fit returns an unphysical negative intercept, so no floor is quoted there

launch_floor.note: Work-independent intercept of latency = a + b*padded_MACs. Two independent sweeps of the shipping configuration agree (85 and 93 us, R2 >= 0.999), so the ~8% spread is the uncertainty on this term. The SAME layer with the swap forced off returns a negative intercept at R2 = 0.98: plain-mapping latency is super-linear in C_out (its re-fetch traffic grows with the problem), so the linear model does not hold there and no floor can be extracted. What sits inside `a`: instruction stream, array start, pipeline fill/drain: is NOT separated by this experiment.
